# Preface {.unnumbered}

## About this book

*Comparative Causal Metrics* is an introduction to **regional impact evaluation** using modern causal-inference methods implemented entirely in **R** and rendered with **Quarto**. The book is organized around a small set of quasi-experimental techniques that have become workhorses for evaluating the effects of policies, shocks, and interventions on regional outcomes:

- **Interrupted time series** — modeling a single region's outcome before and after a discrete event.
- **Regression discontinuity in time** — exploiting sharp temporal cutoffs as natural experiments.
- **Classical synthetic control** — constructing a weighted comparison region from a donor pool.
- **Structural Bayesian time series** — uncertainty-aware counterfactual estimation via state-space models.

Each chapter pairs the conceptual logic of the method with a worked R example using publicly available data, so readers can reproduce every estimate end-to-end.

## How to read this book

The chapters are designed to be read sequentially but each is self-contained. Code is folded by default — click **`</> Code`** in any chapter to reveal the underlying R. The full source is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/cmg777/ccm), and PDF / EPUB downloads are linked in the navbar.

## Acknowledgments

This book builds on the infrastructure of the companion project [*Mastering Causal Metrics*](https://github.com/cmg777/intro2causal) and on a long tradition of applied econometric scholarship.
